title: THE FOUR OLDS audio play — a07_fireworks

lines.sfx: The barn stove ticks with heat and a couple of lawn chairs sit pulled up close to it.
A chair leg scrapes on the bare concrete where the trainer used to stand.
Gunny Tibbs, seventy-one, in his Navy ballcap, pries open a wooden crate at his feet and stands a cardboard tube up on the floor. The rest of them knock together in the crate.

lines.text: Fourth of July stock. Bought it two years before they banned the good ones. Nobody wrote it down anyplace.

lines.sfx: Cricket is over at the coffee pot with his back to him, and the percolator knocks as he sets it down.

lines.text: For what.

lines.sfx: Gunny stands another tube up, harder than he has to, and it thunks on the floor.

lines.text: I did two years on a missile submarine off Alaska, listening for Soviet propellers, so a man like Earl could keep a barn out here no Russian could touch. And they send a fella in a zip-up vest with a sticker gun.
(then) Commies. I don't care what flag they fly over the building.

lines.sfx: Stitch McGrew, seventy-four, has his boots up near the stove, and he turns a tube over and reads the side of it.

lines.text: These'll go four, five hundred feet, easy.

lines.sfx: Dutch Haas, seventy-six, holds a mug he hasn't touched.

lines.text: Three hundred. It's printed on the box.
They always look higher than that once it's good and dark.

lines.sfx: Dutch sets the mug down on the concrete by his boot.

lines.text: I hauled that trainer up from Houston in a horse trailer. Seventy-five. Signed it off a supply captain who wanted it gone off his books.
(then) Fifty years I kept the government's property safe for the government. And they sent a man to take it back like I stole it.

lines.sfx: Gunny taps the side of the crate with his boot.

lines.text: Office locks up at five. That gravel lot out back is empty by dark. Four cases of these up over the parking lot, and we're home before the news.
That's a federal building.
It's a strip mall with a flagpole, Earl.
I've got a grandson who still thinks I hung the moon. I'm not explaining a courtroom to him. Count me out.
Rest of us, then. Friday.

lines.sfx: Cricket sets the pot back on the burner.

lines.text: Do what you're going to do. Just don't tell me about it after.

lines.sfx: Out behind the dark compliance office that night, boots grind across the gravel and then go still.
Stitch braces a tube down inside a length of pipe against a cinder block, and a lighter scrapes and catches.
The fuse hisses. A shell climbs and cracks red over the lot, loud enough to roll back off the buildings.
Then a green one goes up. Then a long gold one hangs there and crackles down slow.
A county truck rolls in slow, the gravel popping under its tires, and a door opens.
Wade Halversen, the deputy, climbs out with his hat already in his hand.

lines.text: Y'all want to tell me whose idea this was, or should I guess?
Mine.
His, but I brought the truck.
I just held the lighter. Following orders.

lines.sfx: One last shell lifts off and pops gold overhead, and not one of the three so much as flinches.
The gold burns down and goes quiet.

lines.text: Anything left in that pipe?
She's cold.

lines.sfx: The next morning a courtroom door thumps shut, and the three of them stand at the table in their pressed shirts.
Judge Benning, seventies, turns over a single sheet of paper up on the bench.

lines.text: How do you gentlemen plead.
Guilty.
Guilty on all of it.
Guilty, Your Honor.

lines.sfx: A young prosecutor pushes his chair back and starts to get up.

lines.text: I was nine years old in my daddy's living room the night men from this state walked on the Moon. Watched it on a television the size of a bread box. Time served. Four hundred dollars each, plus the cost of the gravel. I've got real criminals on this morning's docket, gentlemen. Get on home.

lines.sfx: The gavel cracks down before the prosecutor is all the way up out of his chair.
Out at the bottom of the courthouse steps, Cricket leans on the fender of his pickup, and the three come down the stone steps slow.

lines.text: (to Cricket) Come to gloat?
Came to drive you home.

lines.sfx: Nobody moves for a second. Cricket reaches back and pops the passenger door open.

lines.text: You could've come.
I know it.

lines.sfx: Cricket claps him once, hard, on the shoulder.
The driver's door shuts and the engine turns over.
